title: Minimal local setup
for: A laptop or a single GPU: fine-tune a small model with LoRA, build datasets, and run a first EvalPlus check. Needs Python 3.11 or newer; the macOS system Python 3.9.6 cannot install current TRL.

steps.label: Check the Python version
steps.note: TRL, Transformers, PEFT and Accelerate all declare Requires-Python >=3.11; datasets >=3.10; EvalPlus >=3.9. Install Python 3.11 to 3.13 first (python.org installer, or uv python install 3.12). On Python 3.9, pip only offers TRL up to 0.24.0.

steps.label: Create and activate a virtual environment
steps.command: python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install --upgrade pip
steps.note: Use one environment per training framework.

steps.label: Install the training stack
steps.note: Floors are from TRL's pyproject.toml (transformers>=4.56.2, accelerate>=1.11.0, datasets>=4.7.0, torch>=2.6.0, peft extra >=0.18.0). On 2026-11-25 the latest releases were transformers 5.24.1, datasets 5.2.0, peft 0.22.0, accelerate 1.16.0, trl 1.18.2, and their declared requirements did not conflict. For a CUDA build of torch, follow pytorch.org first.

steps.label: Install the evaluator
steps.note: EvalPlus 0.3.1 (2024-10-20) declares Python >=3.9 and transformers>=4.43.0, datasets>=2.21.0, tree-sitter>=0.22.0. It also pulls openai, anthropic and google-generativeai client packages. Add the vllm extra only on a Linux GPU box.

steps.label: Check the environment
steps.command: pip check && python -c "import transformers, datasets, peft, trl, accelerate; print(transformers.__version__, datasets.__version__, peft.__version__, trl.__version__, accelerate.__version__)"
steps.note: Run this before any training. It catches version conflicts that pip install can leave behind.

steps.label: Log in to the Hub (optional)
steps.note: Needed for gated models and datasets and for pushing checkpoints. The hf CLI comes with huggingface_hub.

steps.label: Smoke-test one SFT run
steps.note: Command from TRL's README. It proves the stack works; swap in your own prompt/completion code dataset and add a peft config for LoRA before a real run.

steps.label: Generate samples, then execute them in Docker
steps.command:
evalplus.codegen --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B --dataset humaneval --backend hf --greedy
docker run --rm --pull=always -v $(pwd)/evalplus_results:/app ganler/evalplus:latest evalplus.evaluate --dataset humaneval --samples /app/humaneval/Qwen--Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B_hf_temp_0.0.jsonl
steps.note: Pattern from EvalPlus's README (safe execution within Docker). The samples filename follows the README's org--model_backend_temp_X.jsonl naming; check the actual file name that codegen wrote. Do not run generated code directly on your laptop.

verified_how: Not installed or run (task rule). Checked 2026-11-25 against: TRL pyproject.toml and README, PyPI JSON requires_python and requires_dist for trl, transformers, peft, accelerate, datasets and evalplus (a script compared each declared version range with the others' latest releases and found no conflict), EvalPlus README, and pip index versions trl on the local Python 3.9.6, which lists only 0.24.0 and so shows the Python floor.

title: Scaling up
for: A multi-GPU node or a Slurm cluster: multi-GPU SFT, vLLM sampling, an RL framework with execution-based rewards, a code sandbox and larger evaluation runs.

steps.label: Create the training environment
steps.note: TRL's extras peft (>=0.18.0) and deepspeed (>=0.18.6) exist in its pyproject. Install a CUDA build of torch matching the cluster first. Keep verl, SkyRL, OpenRLHF and Axolotl in separate environments because they pin different versions.

steps.label: Launch multi-GPU training on one node
steps.command:
accelerate launch --multi_gpu --num_processes 4 train.py
# or, as TRL's docs do:
torchrun --nproc_per_node 8 train.py
steps.note: accelerate launch syntax is from Accelerate's launch tutorial. For ZeRO, set deepspeed="<config.json>" in SFTConfig (TRL's DeepSpeed page) and launch with torchrun, or use: trl sft ... --deepspeed examples/deepspeed_configs/zero2.json from a TRL clone.

steps.label: Submit the same job to Slurm
steps.command:
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:4
export GPUS_PER_NODE=4
accelerate launch --num_processes $GPUS_PER_NODE train.py

# multi-node, from the same example set:
head_node_ip=$(scontrol show hostnames $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST | head -n 1)
LAUNCHER="accelerate launch --num_processes $((SLURM_NNODES * GPUS_PER_NODE)) --num_machines $SLURM_NNODES --rdzv_backend c10d --main_process_ip $head_node_ip --main_process_port 29500"
srun $LAUNCHER train.py
steps.note: Adapted from Accelerate's examples/slurm/submit_multigpu.sh and submit_multinode.sh (those also set job name, output files, cpus-per-task and time, and source an environment). Replace the script with your training script.

steps.label: Start a vLLM sampling server
steps.command:
pip install "trl[vllm]"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs -1
steps.note: From TRL's vLLM integration page. The server and the trainer must run on separate GPUs. For plain sampling or evaluation, the vLLM quickstart shows: uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto, then: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.

steps.label: Run GRPO against that server
steps.note: train.py builds a GRPOTrainer with GRPOConfig(use_vllm=True, vllm_mode="server") and your reward function (TRL docs). For code, make the reward call the sandbox below.

steps.label: Or use a dedicated RL framework (verl)
steps.command:
git clone https://github.com/verl-project/verl && cd verl
UV_RUN="uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra vllm --extra fsdp"
$UV_RUN python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py --local_save_dir ~/data/gsm8k
$UV_RUN python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo data.train_files=$HOME/data/gsm8k/train.parquet data.val_files=$HOME/data/gsm8k/test.parquet data.train_batch_size=256 data.max_prompt_length=512 data.max_response_length=512 actor_rollout_ref.model.path=Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=64 actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4 actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 critic.optim.lr=1e-5 critic.model.path=Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct critic.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 algorithm.kl_ctrl.kl_coef=0.001 trainer.logger=console trainer.val_before_train=False trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 trainer.nnodes=1 trainer.save_freq=10 trainer.test_freq=10 trainer.total_epochs=15 ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.py_executable="${UV_RUN}"
steps.note: From verl's quickstart (GSM8K math, PPO, one GPU with at least 24 GB) with its uv wrapper. verl's uv workflow targets Linux and Python 3.12. For code, point reward.custom_reward_function.path and .name at a compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info) function, as in data/snippets.json verl-grpo-code-reward. Alternatives: SkyRL (docker run -it --runtime=nvidia --gpus all --shm-size=8g --name skyrl novaskyai/skyrl-train-ray-2.57.0-py3.12-cu13.0 /bin/bash, then git clone https://github.com/novasky-ai/SkyRL.git) or OpenRLHF (pip install openrlhf[vllm] inside nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.03-py3, then ray start --head and ray job submit ... python3 -m openrlhf.cli.train_ppo_ray).

steps.label: Run generated code in a sandbox service
steps.command:
docker run -it -p 8080:8080 volcengine/sandbox-fusion:server-20250609
curl 'http://localhost:8080/run_code' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw '{"code": "print(\"Hello, world!\")", "language": "python"}'
steps.note: From SandboxFusion's get-started page (the docs write the host as a site constant; localhost:8080 follows from the -p 8080:8080 mapping). Its docs state no isolation strength, so run it where a breakout is acceptable, or put gVisor or a VM under it.

steps.label: Or use a hardened container per candidate program
steps.command: docker run --rm --network none --read-only --memory 256m --memory-swap 256m --cpus 1 --pids-limit 64 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user 65534:65534 --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=16m -v "$PWD/job:/work:ro" -w /work python:3.12-slim timeout 10 python candidate.py
steps.note: Run on Docker 29.1.3 on 2026-11-24 (data/snippets.json docker-hardened-sandbox). Containers share the host kernel; for adversarial code add gVisor (runsc), a Firecracker microVM, or a hosted sandbox (E2B, Modal).

steps.label: Evaluate at scale
steps.command:
evalplus.codegen --model <your-model> --dataset humaneval --backend vllm --greedy
docker run --rm --pull=always -v $(pwd)/evalplus_results:/app ganler/evalplus:latest evalplus.evaluate --dataset humaneval --samples /app/humaneval/<samples-file>.jsonl

uv tool install harbor
harbor run --dataset terminal-bench@2.0 --agent claude-code --model anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 --n-concurrent 4
steps.note: EvalPlus (pip install "evalplus[vllm]") and Harbor commands are from their READMEs. Harbor needs Python 3.12, Docker and a model API key; it runs tasks in local Docker by default and on cloud sandboxes with --env.

verified_how: Not run (no GPUs, no installs, per the task rules). Every command was copied from the named project's README or docs read on 2026-11-25 (TRL vLLM and DeepSpeed pages, Accelerate launch tutorial and Slurm examples, vLLM quickstart, verl install and quickstart pages, SkyRL installation docs, OpenRLHF README, SandboxFusion get-started page, EvalPlus and Harbor READMEs); the hardened Docker command was run on 2026-11-24. Slurm and multi-node scripts are condensed from the Accelerate examples and need your cluster's modules, partitions and time limits.
